body.input: Which defence and drone companies opened an office in Denmark in 2026?

response.content:
## Defence and Drone Companies That Opened (or Prepared to Open) an Office in Denmark in 2026

### 1. TEKEVER
European defence technology company **TEKEVER** established its first Nordic base in **Odense** in November 2026. The company develops AI-powered autonomous drone systems for defence, security, and civil applications, and has logged more than 50,000 operational flight hours in Ukraine. Odense was chosen for its internationally recognised drone and robotics ecosystem.

### 2. Fire Point (Ukraine)
Ukrainian defence company **Fire Point**, which leads the FREYJA European anti-ballistic missile defence programme, prepared to open a **programme office in Copenhagen**. On 11 November 2026, President Zelenskyy announced before the Danish parliament that preparations were complete. The office will coordinate work with companies from the 11 participating nations. Fire Point is also building a rocket fuel factory near the Danish town of Vojens.

### 3. Skyfall (Ukraine) — in discussions
Ukrainian drone manufacturer **Skyfall** entered talks with the Danish government in February 2026 about establishing production on Danish soil. If finalised, Skyfall would become the second Ukrainian defence firm (after Fire Point) to set up operations in Denmark. As of the latest reports, formal agreements on a specific office or factory location had not yet been publicly confirmed.

# TEKEVER Establishes Its First Nordic Base in Odense

Nov 10, 2026 | Articles, News, News from the city of Odense, Press Releases, Robotics and Drones, Seed and Venture Capital

European defence technology company TEKEVER has chosen Odense as the location for its first operational presence in the Nordic region. The establishment strengthens Odense’s position as a leading European hub for drone technology, robotics, and defence innovation while creating new opportunities for collaboration across the Danish ecosystem.

### A strategic platform for the Nordics [...] ### A strategic platform for the Nordics

TEKEVER is one of Europe’s leading defence technology companies, developing AI-powered autonomous systems for defence, security, and civil applications. Its drone systems have logged more than 50,000 operational flight hours in Ukraine, and the company has secured major long-term defence programmes in countries including Germany, the United Kingdom, and Portugal.

With its new base in Odense, TEKEVER aims to support activities across the Nordic region while strengthening collaboration with Danish industry, research institutions, and public partners. The Danish operation will be developed in phases as demand grows, becoming part of TEKEVER’s wider European network spanning Portugal, the UK, France, Germany, and Estonia. [...] ### Chosen for its drone and robotics ecosystem

Odense was selected for its internationally recognised drone and robotics ecosystem, which provides access to specialised talent, testing facilities, research capabilities, and industry partners.

Key assets include Odense Robotics, UAS Denmark Test Center, and the University of Southern Denmark’s SDU Drone Center and Flight Lab. Together, they have helped establish the city as one of Europe’s leading environments for autonomous systems and advanced robotics.

TEKEVER is already engaging with Danish partners and sees significant opportunities for future collaboration across defence, security, and advanced technology development.

The Ukrainian president said his country needs the Freyja system “by winter to see how the system works.”

  Asked about the purpose of establishing an office in Copenhagen, Zelenskyy gave a brief answer: “Managing.”

  He explained that the office would bring together representatives from several countries who would work with different companies involved in the project.

  Zelenskyy also said he would inspect a Danish radar on Wednesday that forms part of the Freyja system.

  Similar discussions are underway about opening an office in Oslo, Norway, he added.

  The Freyja project is led by Ukrainian defence company Fire Point, which is developing the system in cooperation with European defence manufacturers. [...] Fire Point, a Ukrainian defense company, leads the project and is developing it alongside European defense firms. The company is currently building a factory near the Danish town of Vojens to produce rocket fuel. In August, the company stated that this fuel will be used for the FP-7.x, the interceptor missile designed for the Freya system.

  A Danish company, Weibel, has also developed a radar using Doppler technology that can track ballistic missiles. These weapons are especially fast and hard for Ukraine to defend against because Ukraine has run out of missiles. The Weibel radar could become part of the Freya system.

  Bruus did not state in the interview whether his plans mean setting up more production beyond the factory that is already planned. [...] Fire Point is also establishing a factory in Denmark with support from the Danish government.

  Zelenskyy’s visit to Denmark was announced Tuesday morning. It is his fifth visit to the country since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

  During Tuesday’s visit, he participated in a joint interview with Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen at the University of Copenhagen.

  He also attended a meeting with Nordic heads of government at Marienborg, the Danish prime minister’s official residence.

  On Wednesday, Zelenskyy is scheduled to meet King Frederik and address the Folketing, Denmark’s Parliament.
